# Accuracy corpus and methodology (2.6.2 WS-E)

Research by Bakr Fayez

## What lives here

- `corpus.py` — corpus construction and the labeling file
  FORMAT (schema 1, documented in the module docstring).
- `run_accuracy.py` — the metrics runner. Writes
  `tests/benchmarks/accuracy-2.6.2.json` when invoked with
  `--out`. The JSON contains role labels and counts only —
  never fixture file names, paths, or hashes.

## Corpora

**Synthetic** — samples generated by the repo's synthetic
builders (`tests/synthetic_fixtures.py`, the synthetic
framework fixture set, and endpoint samples constructed
per class in `corpus.py`). Ground truth is builder intent
or the construction itself.

**Real** — local fixtures bound by role through
`$NAR_FIXTURES/manifest.env`. Labels derive from prior
verified analysis (the positive role bindings) plus
cross-labeling:

- a real fixture of one engine family is a real NEGATIVE
  for every other family's detector;
- the clean set, and every real fixture with no recorded
  protection attribution, is a NEGATIVE for attributed
  commercial-packer detection.

The labeling data itself — which local file carries which
label — lives locally with the fixtures, never in this
repo. An optional local labeling file
(`$NAR_FIXTURES/labeling.json`, schema 1 as documented in
`corpus.py`) can be merged by the operator; the runner
states in its methodology line whether one was present.

## Metrics discipline

Per analyzer: samples / positives / negatives / TP / FP /
FN / TN / unclassified + precision / recall / F1 / accuracy
/ FPR / FNR; a confusion matrix for the multiclass format
analyzer. Unclassified (tool failure) positives count as
misses and are also reported separately. A rate with a
zero denominator is `null`, never invented. Synthetic and
real results are always reported separately and never
pooled. An analyzer without defensible ground truth is
NOT MEASURED with the reason stated — no estimate is ever
substituted.
